A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same annotation and bias-auditing study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-model evaluations, LAION-400M demographic and association analyses, and CLIP and Stable Diffusion bias-transfer experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds human validation, quantitative caption comparisons, CC12M statistics, and additional bias-transfer analyses.

M1.justification: The YOLO detection and filtering procedure, consensus-based SigLIP classifiers, InternVL3-8B caption generation, and SAE/PMI pipeline are retained. The additions evaluate and diagnose these methods without changing the annotation procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage expands through an external demographic-composition audit of CC12M (G.4) and sentiment/crime-word evaluation of generated person captions (F). These extend the existing web-image/text bias-auditing domain; earlier datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: G.3 adds cubic Chebyshev fits for comparison with the retained linear bias-transfer fits. The caption-model comparison still evaluates InternVL3-2B/8B and Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B; GPT-5.1 is introduced as their evaluator, not as another captioning baseline.

E3.justification: Caption evaluation changes from qualitative inspection of 4,939 bounding boxes to pairwise GPT-5.1 judgments on 500. Section 3 adds a 200-image detection check by one annotator and a stratified 648-image demographic-label study with two annotators. G.3 and G.5 introduce polynomial-fit and focused word-group evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds human-label error analysis, race/ethnicity logit correlations, generated-caption bias diagnostics, nonlinear-fit sensitivity analysis, and crime/personality subgroup analyses. These examine annotation validity, possible classifier bias, and limits of linear transfer. The small LAION detection case-study panel from v1 Figure 13b is removed.

E5.justification: v2 Figures 8–9 add 95% confidence intervals to the previously reported correlation and R-squared estimates, such as R-squared 0.71 with interval [0.69, 0.72]. The PDFs do not document the interval-construction procedure or establish additional repeated runs.

E6.justification: New results include 82.5% fully correct detection images and race/ethnicity agreement of kappa 0.638 for human–classifier versus 0.654 between humans. InternVL3-8B wins 75.6%, 63.0%, and 58.2% against Qwen2.5-VL-3B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and InternVL3-2B, respectively. New polynomial CLIP fits yield R-squared 0.61, 0.67, and 0.73; crime/personality linear fits yield 0.12 and 0.10. CC12M and caption-bias results are also added, while the original headline linear-fit values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The SAE/PMI definitions, conditional-independence assumption, probability decomposition, and CLIP bias equation are unchanged. Moving the main-text PMI equation inline and renumbering equations do not alter the mathematics. The polynomial addition supplies empirical fits without new proofs or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the annotation-resource, harmful-association, SAE-analysis, and 60–70% linear-fit claims. Replacing 'linearly explained' with 'predicted by a linear fit' preserves the statistical meaning already specified through R-squared in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of classifier-conditioned human sampling, subjective demographic judgments, contextual gender-label errors, and possible Black/unclear confusion. It also interprets nonlinear patterns, qualifies transfer for specific word groups, argues for CC12M generalizability, and discusses possible sources of caption bias. Its new conclusion that captions are 'overall safe' extends beyond the earlier discussion; Appendix A's existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement replaces the promised code release with a specific GitHub link and reports data availability. Appendix F supplies the complete caption-judging prompt and GPT-5.1 reasoning setting, while Appendix D adds consensus-pool counts. Existing classifier training details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Changpinyo et al. (2021) for CC12M and Rudman et al. (2012) for personality traits. The main related-work discussion and Appendix H retain their prior research positioning.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and section organization are retained. Local changes include a human-validation block, a discussion paragraph, new G.3–G.5 subsections, revised caption-evaluation prose, predictive wording, and conference-header and acknowledgement edits. There is no extensive rewriting of retained material.

P2.justification: v2 adds human-agreement matrices, a logit-correlation heatmap, caption-bias bars, nonlinear-fit plots, CC12M distributions, and subgroup plots. Existing transfer plots gain interval annotations and shaded bands. Example faces are blurred or regenerated, the LAION detection panel is removed, and several retained displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: The direct human checks address an important validation gap: v1's in-domain race/ethnicity evaluation relied on model-consensus labels. This substantially strengthens the central annotation resource, while quantitative caption assessment and subgroup analyses improve support and clarify applicability. Undocumented confidence-interval construction and an overly broad caption-safety conclusion remain weaknesses, but do not outweigh the validation gains.
